transcription:tinfoil.name: Tinfoil

deferral.why: Not resource-blocked and not a matter of finishing incomplete work -- implementing this client as a plain HTTPS POST would defeat Tinfoil's entire proposition, which is an attested enclave verified before any audio is sent. This manifest's statusVocabulary has no 'declined on principle' term; temporarily-deferred is used only because it is the closest status that does not assert a working implementation exists (which the previous status, rewired-to-direct-byok, did). 'Temporarily' should not be read literally: nothing here is scheduled to change absent a decision to build an attestation-verifying client, which has not been made.
dependencies: an attestation-verifying HTTP client that fetches and checks Tinfoil's attestation document against a hardware root of trust before any request is sent -- a distinct verification step, not a REST client feature
a decision that this project wants to build one, which has not been made
deferral.interface: crates/transcription-core::route::ProviderClientKind::Tinfoil is the enum member every match must cover; clients::why_tinfoil_is_refused() names the reason and clients::shape() returns TranscriptionError::ClientNotImplemented for it. No attested-client module exists.

transcription:tinfoil.note: Status corrected by Task 19's audit of every ACTIVE-vocabulary entry: this previously carried rewired-to-direct-byok, which verify-parity.mjs treats as asserting a working implementation, while clients.rs returns TranscriptionError::ClientNotImplemented for Tinfoil and nothing else implements it -- the same pattern platform:aec was already corrected for. Deliberately unreachable, not unfinished, for the reason in `deferral.why`: Tinfoil's proposition is an attested enclave, and a plain HTTPS POST to the same host would transcribe correctly and provide none of that while appearing in the UI as Tinfoil -- a confidentiality claim the request did not earn. route.rs already refuses a Tinfoil host configured as a custom endpoint for this reason.

local-asr:nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6.name: Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B
local-asr:nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6.note: Reachable since 2026-09-01. Both blockers this entry ever had are gone, and they were different blockers: first there was no client for sherpa's streaming WebSocket protocol (KNEG-84 wrote one, measured against the real server), and then there was no pin (KNEG-118 downloaded and hashed it here: sha256 c6bf5e0d..., 475,271,763 bytes, extracting to 14 files and 684,574,872 bytes). Downloaded twice by accident, and both runs produced the same digest -- an unplanned reproducibility control. Reachable the same way as its English sibling: install it under Settings > Transcription > Local and choose 'Use for meetings', which writes meetings.streamModel for meeting-stream:local-streaming to read. Driven on the real server the same day and it transcribed its own German sample (test_wavs/de.wav) over an identical protocol: cumulative text, is_final and is_eof both turning true on the last frame, then TEXT Done!. So 'the same wire as its English sibling' is measured rather than inferred, which matters because that inference was the only thing this entry rested on. It is the only multilingual option in the local streaming path: fifteen languages against the English model's one. What is NOT verified: a meeting through it. The probe drove the server with a WAV; nobody has recorded with it, and no language other than German has been tried.

local-asr:nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.name: Nemotron Speech Streaming EN 0.6B
local-asr:nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.note: Reachable since 2026-09-01, and this is the model the streaming protocol was measured against. Pinned in config/provider-registry.json from bytes that moved through a real machine (sha256 78e2b79f..., 463,945,051 bytes, extracting to 9 files). It installs on the same screen as the Parakeet pair and is chosen for meetings rather than dictation, because it is a streaming model: Settings > Transcription > Local offers 'Use for meetings', which writes meetings.streamModel, and meeting-stream:local-streaming reads it. The protocol was measured on 2026-09-01 with crates/meeting-core/examples/sherpa_ws_probe.rs against the real server and the real reference client, both directions, with the reference client reproducing the model's own test_wavs/trans.txt first as the control. Three facts are in no documentation and one contradicts it: samples are f32 little-endian (the reference client's --help says 16-bit), the transcript text is cumulative per segment, and the server never closes the socket. A malformed frame draws no reply at all, so this provider has no error channel and fault::FaultKind::Reported is unreachable for it. A real meeting was recorded through it on 2026-09-01 and the words arrived as spoken. What is NOT verified: the saved note, which comes from a separate whole-file pass rather than from the live partials.

meeting-stream:corti-realtime.note: Reachable: a key is stored on Settings > Providers and the provider itself is chosen on Settings > Meetings. Corrected 2026-08-27: this previously also claimed the environment and tenant were chosen on Settings > Meetings -- false. Neither field appears on that screen at all; both are entered only on Settings > Transcription (`corti_environment`/`corti_tenant`, SettingsTranscription.tsx), and the only command that writes them is `dictation_set_cloud_provider`, behind the "Use for dictation" button -- which also sets `cloud_transcription_provider = "corti"`, `use_local_whisper = false` and `transcription_mode = "providers"`. So configuring Corti's meeting tenancy today means repointing dictation at Corti first; there is no independent path. Keyterms travel inside the session-config message (`configuration.keyterms`, KeytermWire::SessionConfig). Two different confidence levels here, not one: the OAuth2 token exchange reuses kw_transcription_core::clients::corti_token_endpoint/corti_token_request, already implemented and tested for batch Corti transcription -- reused, not believed. The socket wire is a different matter: the endpoint path, the message envelope, and most of the session-config block beyond `configuration.keyterms` have no vendor source anywhere in this repository -- they were invented, not read from documentation, and the implementer said so directly. No live call has been made -- no Corti credential exists on this machine. See docs/PLATFORM_SUPPORT.md for the full breakdown.

meeting-stream:openai-realtime.note: Two WebSockets, one per capture, because this provider labels no speakers and one socket would make AudioSource on every event a guess. 24 kHz only, which is why the meeting pipeline resamples per session. Sixty-minute server cap, so a longer meeting reconnects and MeetingTranscript::reconnects says how often. Keyterms are accepted and ignored upstream, so none are sent. **Verified live on 2026-08-28**: a real meeting transcribed through this client, microphone and system audio, against OpenAI's GA Realtime API. The first cloud meeting client in this project to meet a server. Getting there took five live attempts and five fixes -- the retired beta header, transcription_session.update -> session.update, the session.created/updated event names, the required session.type, and the audio config moving under audio.input. Every one was named by the server itself once the close reason stopped being discarded; see docs/BENCH_CHECK.md.

meeting-stream:local-streaming.name: Local streaming model
meeting-stream:local-streaming.note: New relative to meeting-stream:local, and what that entry's note said was blocked. sherpa-onnx-online-websocket-server on loopback, two sockets, one per capture -- words as they are recognised rather than a five-second window three seconds late. The protocol was measured on 2026-09-01 with crates/meeting-core/examples/sherpa_ws_probe.rs against the real server and the real reference client, both directions, with the reference client reproducing the model's own test_wavs/trans.txt first as the control. Three facts are in no documentation and one contradicts it: samples are f32 little-endian (the reference client's --help says 16-bit), the transcript text is cumulative per segment, and the server never closes the socket. A malformed frame draws no reply at all, so this provider has no error channel and fault::FaultKind::Reported is unreachable for it. Reachable: pick a streaming model under Settings > Transcription > Local (it writes meetings.streamModel) and choose 'Local streaming model' on Settings > Meetings. The server is started when a meeting starts, not at launch. **Run against a real meeting on 2026-09-01** and the words arrive as they are spoken, which is the whole difference from meeting-stream:local. What that run did not cover: Stop and transcribe, and the saved note -- the live transcript and the saved one come from different passes, so words on screen say nothing about what ends up in the note.

diarization-model:3dspeaker-campplus-en.name: CAM++ Speaker Embedding (English)
diarization-model:3dspeaker-campplus-en.note: Measured and built 2026-09-01 (KNEG-73a). This entry carried a `deferral` block naming three dependencies -- the `ort` crate, a `sherpa-onnx-diarize` sidecar, and silero_vad.onnx -- and all three were wrong. The pinned sherpa release already ships sherpa-onnx-offline-speaker-diarization beside the offline transcription CLI this project drives for Parakeet, that binary links ONNX Runtime itself, and the pyannote segmentation model does its own voice-activity detection, so no separate VAD model is involved. The implementation is therefore the same shape as kw_transcription_core::sherpa: a pure half (kw_meeting_core::diarization -- build_args, interpret, assign) and a thin Command half. Both models are pinned by measurement, and both digests are re-readable by tools/model-pin/pin.mjs --verify and --verify-stated. WHAT IS MEASURED: the CLI's argument set, its output shape, that a failure and a silent recording produce byte-identical stdout so the exit status is the only discriminator, that speaker labels are cluster indices which are not dense from zero, and that turns overlap and can nest. WHAT IS NOT: whether the speaker turns are right in a real meeting. One voice cannot be confused with another, so the integration test's one-speaker control proves the flags and the renumbering and nothing about attribution -- that is a by-hand check. AND ONE LIMIT WORTH READING: the embedding model is language-sensitive where the segmentation model is not, measured by running the same Chinese reference recording through an English and a Chinese embedding model and getting three speakers against four. Only the English model is pinned, so English is the measured case. REACHABLE since 2026-09-01 (KNEG-124): Settings > Meetings > Speaker labels installs both models, reports which of the runtime and the two models is missing rather than one 'not ready', and carries the two measured caveats -- the 8%-of-the-recording cost and that the speaker model is English-only. The consumer is meeting.rs's whole-recording pass, which now keeps Inference::Timed's segments instead of discarding them; a note whose labels could not be produced says so rather than arriving unlabelled and silent.

calendar:google.note: Reachable: Settings > Calendar offers Google Calendar one-click Connect using an app-owned desktop PKCE client or Advanced custom override. The Google desktop secret is public and sent only on token and refresh grants; custom secrets and OAuth tokens live in the OS credential store. Calendar v3 calendarList and expanded events.list use snapshots over [now - 24 hours, now + 30 days), committed per calendar; failed pages keep its cache. The client was registered on 2026-11-13, and a development build carrying it connected a personal Google account and synced it; no release build has carried it. Other evidence is unit tests and dev-fixture screenshots. Local Upcoming readers, Meetings Upcoming/event picker and recording links are built and fixture-tested, still unverified against real accounts. See docs/CALENDAR_PROVIDER_SETUP.md, R12.

calendar:microsoft.note: Reachable: Settings > Calendar offers Outlook (Outlook.com, Hotmail and Microsoft 365) one-click Connect using an app-owned public PKCE client or Advanced custom client, never a client secret. Requests use login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com v1.0 me/calendars and me/calendars/{id}/calendarView, with UTC snapshots over [now - 24 hours, now + 30 days). A page failure keeps that calendar cache. The client was registered on 2026-11-13, and a development build carrying it connected a personal Outlook.com account and synced it; a Microsoft 365 work account stopped at its tenant's administrator-approval screen, and no release build has carried it. Other evidence is unit tests and dev-fixture screenshots. See docs/CALENDAR_PROVIDER_SETUP.md, R12.

There is no macOS machine in this development environment to write or verify that binding against. kw_calendar_core::apple describes the shape a future implementation would fill in (AppleCalendarSource) but implements none of it -- unlike the two Tinfoil entries, this is a genuine resource gap, not a principled refusal: nothing here says Apple Calendar should not be supported, only that it cannot be built or verified on this machine.

EventKit Rust bindings, which do not exist anywhere in this project
a macOS machine to write and verify the binding against, which is not available in this development environment

calendar:apple.note: Status corrected by Task 19's audit of every ACTIVE-vocabulary entry: this previously carried status "platform-specific", which verify-parity.mjs treats as asserting a working implementation exists for the platforms it names, while apple.rs's own module doc says AppleCalendarSource is deliberately unimplemented by anything in this crate, on every platform including macOS -- the identical pattern platform:aec was already corrected for. Integrations > Calendar reported it as Unsupported with that reason until 2026-11-24, when the row was removed (KNEG-571): a row that could only say "Not supported yet" is not a setting. calendar_status still returns the reason. Implementing it needs a macOS build of this application and EventKit bindings, neither of which exists; unverifiable on this development machine even once written.

developer:local-rest-api.note: Upstream is a good model: loopback-only, 0600 discovery file, timingSafeEqual bearer, 1 MB body cap, 15 routes under /v1/. Port nearly as-is.

developer:cli.note: NOT a port. The CLI is a separate npm package absent from the repo; only its documented noun-verb surface and exit codes 0-4 survive as a spec. Integrations > CLI now tells a user it exists, where the compiled binary was actually found (or that it was not), and the discovery file's real permission state.

developer:mcp.note: NOT a port. Upstream MCP is a hosted Streamable-HTTP service; no local or stdio implementation exists in the checkout. Entirely new work: tools/knegiswhisper-mcp is a stdio server reusing the CLI's own client and discovery-file reader over the local API, and Integrations > MCP shows the exact command line to configure in a client plus whether the binary was actually found.

developer:agent-skills.note: Written 2026-08-31 (KNEG-85): docs/agent-skills/ holds knegiswhisper-api/SKILL.md and knegiswhisper-cli/SKILL.md, covering the loopback HTTP API, the knegiswhisper command and the knegiswhisper-mcp stdio server. This entry claimed "ported" for a twenty-task run against a directory that had never existed; the gate that should have caught that only checked the target was named, and now checks it exists and is not empty (KNEG-86, rule documentation-target-missing). meeting-detect:zoom.note: Zoom.exe means the client is open; CptHost.exe exists only during a call, and only the latter offers to record. Neither name has been seen to match yet -- see docs/PLATFORM_SUPPORT.md.

meeting-detect:teams.note: Offered when it is in a call, and detected by the microphone rather than by a process. New Teams runs the call inside ms-teams.exe and spawns nothing, measured with meeting_detect_probe on 2026-08-26, which left it unofferable: the only signal was 'the client is open', true from login wherever Teams starts with Windows. mic_users_probe measured the difference on 2026-09-01 -- Teams open and idle holds no capture session, Teams in a call holds one, each run controlled by a second process that had to appear. Windows only; elsewhere the capture list is empty and Teams stays reported rather than offered.

meeting-detect:webex.note: webexmta.exe is the in-call process. Not seen to match yet -- see docs/PLATFORM_SUPPORT.md.

meeting-detect:facetime.note: macOS only, and compiled out elsewhere rather than silently absent. Like Teams it has no separate in-call process, and unlike Teams it has no second signal either: microphone activity is read through IAudioSessionManager2 and nothing equivalent is read on macOS. Reported, not offered.

meeting-detect:generic.note: Process allow/blocklist only, user-editable. Upstream also covered calendar events, microphone activity and system-audio activity: calendars are chunk F and microphone activity needs the IAudioSessionManager2 listener, which is unwritten. Named rather than left implied, because a half-built detector that looks whole is how somebody comes to trust one that misses half their meetings. Browser meetings such as Google Meet are covered by the allowlist plus manual capture; no per-tab detector is possible.

media:audio-import.note: Backend corrected by Task 19: this named crates/notes-core, which holds no import code; the real implementation is MediaImportRuntime::import_local_file in media.rs.

media:video-import.note: Backend corrected by Task 19, same as media:audio-import: MediaImportRuntime::import_local_file serves both audio and video, since ffmpeg strips both to 16 kHz mono WAV and there is nothing else to tell them apart.

media:url-import.note: Disabled until every resolved address, redirect, and extractor-generated request made by yt-dlp can be checked against the network policy. The dormant backend is not registered as a Tauri command.

media:openwhispr-import.note: storage::import::from_openwhispr: opens an existing OpenWhispr transcriptions.db through a second, read-only connection, introspects its columns with pragma table_info rather than assuming upstream's ~70-ALTER-TABLE schema, drops every cloud/sync column and both plaintext token tables (relocating the tokens into the OS credential store instead), and fills notes_fts through triggers as notes are inserted. Implemented and tested from early in the build; deliberately absent from this manifest until it had a screen, which it now does. The screen renders the full ImportReport -- what copied, what was skipped and why, which tables were not copied with row counts, which rows deleted in OpenWhispr were passed over, which columns were dropped per table, and which credentials moved -- never the credential values.

search:sqlite-fts.note: FTS5 external-content table mirroring notes via three triggers. Port verbatim. The search itself is kw_notes_core::notes::search (crates/notes-core/src/notes.rs:255), which is what `backend` now names; the virtual table and its three triggers are declared in crates/storage/migrations/0001_initial.sql:110-133. `backend` read crates/storage until 2026-09-01, which named where the table is created rather than where the query runs -- the same class of drift as search:semantic's `interface` field below, and found in the same pass (KNEG-73).

deferral.why: Re-checked 2026-09-01 (KNEG-73) and narrowed rather than dissolved. Of the four checkable claims this block made, two were false on their face. ONNX Runtime is not a barrier: onnxruntime.dll is already in the tree and installed on this machine, inside the pinned sherpa archive -- the same discovery that collapsed diarization's identical claim on the same day. The `ort` crate is a dependency of one design and not of the feature: kw_meeting_core::diarization drives an ONNX model with no `ort` anywhere in Cargo.lock, by shelling out to a sherpa binary that links the runtime itself. What is genuinely absent is a vector store and a pinned text-embedding model. The judgement is unchanged -- a vector store is a large dependency for a feature the application must work without anyway -- but it is now the only argument left rather than one of three, and the installer, digest-pin and verify machinery such a model would need already ships for diarization-model:3dspeaker-campplus-en.
dependencies: a vector store: no qdrant sidecar in config/sidecars.json, and no in-process alternative in Cargo.lock
a pinned text-embedding model -- all-MiniLM-L6-v2 or an equivalent: none is pinned by tools/model-pin, and none appears in config/provider-registry.json or anywhere else
deferral.interface: None is declared anywhere in this repository. The previous value, notes_core::search::SemanticIndex, named a module that has never existed -- crates/notes-core/src is lib.rs, notes.rs and transcript.rs, and SemanticIndex appears nowhere in the tree but in this manifest. The function semantic ranking would have to join is kw_notes_core::notes::search (crates/notes-core/src/notes.rs:255), whose SearchHit is id, title and snippet, with no score field to rank by.
deferral.degradation: Nothing degrades, because nothing was built to degrade from. FTS5 keyword search is the whole of search today rather than a fallback from something richer. The previous value claimed the UI hides semantic ranking rather than failing; apps/desktop/src contains zero occurrences of `semantic`, so there has never been anything to hide.

search:semantic.note: Note added 2026-08-27, in the whole-branch review's fix wave: this entry has carried `temporarily-deferred` with a `deferral` block since before this plan began, but no top-level `note` explaining why -- unlike every other deferred entry in this file. The reason is docs/BUILD_PLAN.md's chunk I: the Qdrant sidecar, MiniLM embeddings and `ort` crate this needs were not attempted across the 19 tasks in this plan or the one added mid-run; `search:sqlite-fts` is fully functional and is what the UI falls back to in the meantime. This entry sits outside both the ACTIVE-status audit's scope (it never claimed a working implementation, so there was nothing to overclaim) and the parity gate's `USER_CONFIGURABLE` set, so no gate would ever have caught the missing note on its own. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-01 (KNEG-73): the deferral block above was corrected in place rather than annotated, the way the two diarization entries were on the same day, and the sentence just above about the UI falling back overstates it in the same way the old `degradation` field did -- FTS5 is not a fallback, it is all there has ever been. WHAT IS MEASURED: onnxruntime.dll ships inside the pinned sherpa archive and is extracted by the installer (docs/BENCH_CHECK.md:1290 counts the 23 extracted files by name on Windows); there is no `ort` in Cargo.lock; `qdrant` appears nowhere in this repository but in this entry's own prose; no text-embedding model is pinned anywhere; notes_core::search does not exist and never has; and apps/desktop/src contains no occurrence of `semantic`. WHAT IS NOT: whether semantic ranking would actually beat FTS5 on a corpus of this application's notes -- nobody has tried it, and no version of this entry has ever claimed a measurement; and whether an in-process vector store would remove the sidecar dependency altogether, which is a design question nobody has costed. It stays deferred on the narrowed ground and nothing was built for it -- no sidecar, no embedding path, no search module. The general defect this entry is the worked example of: verify-parity.mjs checks that a deferred entry HAS `why`, `dependencies`, `interface` and `expectedPhase`, and has no way to check that any of them is still true, which is how this one named a nonexistent module for months.
